design_note: Focused prompts for API availability, false passes, migration semantics and scope. Use only the prompts affected by a guidance change; a few independent with-skill/without-skill spot checks are sufficient. Build and run generated tests separately where behavior matters. No web/documentation lookup during a skill-isolation spot check. tests/run.sh validates executable samples, not model performance.

evals.name: xctassert-interop-trap
evals.prompt: We're mid-migration from XCTest to Swift Testing and some @Test functions still call XCTAssertEqual inside them. We just updated to Xcode 27 (Swift 6.4), but our Package.swift still says swift-tools-version: 6.0. Are failures from those XCTAssertEqual calls actually failing our tests? If not, how do we make them count without migrating everything today?
evals.expected_output: Explains the ST-0021 interop modes: with tools-version < 6.4 the default is Limited mode where XCTAssert failures produce warnings but the test still passes; Complete mode (tools-version >= 6.4 or SWIFT_TESTING_XCTEST_INTEROP_MODE=complete) makes them real failures; recommends #expect/#require as the durable fix
expectations: States that with swift-tools-version < 6.4 on Swift 6.4 the XCTAssert failures do NOT fail the test by default (they surface as warnings under Limited interop mode, or are ignored on older toolchains) — an answer claiming they simply fail, or that they are still completely silent on this setup, fails this assertion
Names a working mechanism to make them count: raising swift-tools-version to 6.4+ or setting SWIFT_TESTING_XCTEST_INTEROP_MODE=complete (ST-0021 interop modes)
Recommends migrating the assertions to #expect/#require as the proper fix rather than relying on interop

evals.name: image-attachment
evals.prompt: In a Swift Testing test I want to attach a UIImage screenshot to the test results when my snapshot comparison fails, so I can see what was rendered. We're on Xcode 26.6 (Swift 6.3). What's the right way to do this?
evals.expected_output: Attachment.record(image, named:, as: .png) inside the failure branch of the comparison — images attach directly since Swift 6.3 (ST-0014/0017, AttachableAsImage); no manual PNG encoding; no failure-only attachment trait exists, so record conditionally
expectations: Recommends attaching the UIImage directly via the Attachment API with an image format (e.g. Attachment.record(screenshot, named:, as: .png)) as available in Swift 6.3
Does not present manually encoding the image to Data (pngData()/jpegData()) as the required or primary approach
Mentions format control (AttachableImageFormat / .png / .jpeg with encoding quality) or the correct availability context (Swift 6.3 toolchain; iOS 14+ floor)

Records the attachment only when the snapshot comparison fails (for example inside an if/else on the comparison result), as the prompt asks; does not invent a trait or option that saves attachments only for failing tests

evals.name: repeating-trait-trap
evals.prompt: I have a flaky Swift Testing test and I want to run it repeatedly until it fails so I can catch it in the act. I remember something like @Test(.repeating(.untilFailure, maximumIterations: 100)) — what's the exact trait syntax? We're on Xcode 27.
evals.expected_output: No .repeating trait exists. Use Xcode's test repetition (test plan or scheme test options, e.g. repeat until failure) or, in Swift 6.4, swift test --repeat-until fail --maximum-repetitions 100 (ST-0024, per-test-case semantics)
expectations: Clearly states that no .repeating trait exists in Swift Testing (it is only a future direction in ST-0024) — an answer providing any trait-based repetition syntax fails this assertion
Provides a real mechanism: Xcode's test repetition options (test plan or scheme, until failure) and/or swift test --repeat-until fail --maximum-repetitions N (Swift 6.4)
Does not invent other non-existent APIs (e.g. Test.currentIteration, a repetition parameter on @Test) as available

evals.name: mid-test-skip
evals.prompt: In XCTest I could `throw XCTSkip("server unreachable")` in the middle of a test when a runtime precondition wasn't met. What's the Swift Testing equivalent for bailing out of an already-running test? Swift 6.3 toolchain. Also: what happens if I do this inside a parameterized test?
evals.expected_output: try Test.cancel("reason") — ST-0016, Swift 6.3; in parameterized tests it cancels only the current test case; .disabled(if:)/.enabled(if:) remain the pre-start alternatives
expectations: Recommends try Test.cancel("reason") as the runtime equivalent, available since Swift 6.3 (ST-0016)
States that in a parameterized test, Test.cancel cancels only the current test case while other cases continue
Distinguishes it from pre-start conditions (.disabled(if:) / .enabled(if:)) which prevent the test from starting at all

evals.name: issue-severity-warning
evals.prompt: I want to log a non-fatal warning from inside a Swift Testing test — something visible in the test results, but that doesn't fail the test (e.g. 'image match 93%, above threshold but not identical'). Is that possible? Swift 6.3 toolchain.
evals.expected_output: Issue.record("message", severity: .warning) — ST-0013, Swift 6.3; warnings appear in results without failing the test; default severity is .error which fails
expectations: States it is possible via Issue.record with severity: .warning, available since Swift 6.3 (ST-0013) — an answer claiming all recorded issues fail the test fails this assertion
Explains the warning appears in test results but the test still passes
Notes the default severity is .error (which fails the test) or mentions the isFailure distinction

evals.name: transferable-attachment
evals.prompt: My document type conforms to Transferable (CoreTransferable) and can export PDF. Can I attach it to a Swift Testing test result directly, and what are the exact version requirements — toolchain and OS?
evals.expected_output: Yes — try await Attachment(exporting:as:) (ST-0023, Swift 6.4), async throwing initializer; OS floor iOS 18.2/macOS 15.2 from CoreTransferable; on older floors encode manually and attach Data
expectations: States that direct Transferable attachment exists via an async throwing Attachment initializer (Attachment(exporting:as:)), added in Swift 6.4 (ST-0023) — not the synchronous record family
States the OS availability floor (iOS 18.2 / macOS 15.2 era releases) in addition to the Swift 6.4 toolchain requirement
Offers a fallback for older deployment targets (export/encode manually and attach the resulting Data)

evals.name: migrate-xctestcase
evals.expected_output: Teardown still resets PriceCache.shared (deinit on a final class or actor suite, or an equivalent scope such as a TestScoping trait); every parallel user of PriceCache.shared is grouped under one serialized parent or given an independent resource, and per-suite .serialized is not presented as global isolation; cart becomes a non-optional stored property; continueAfterFailure = false turns every assertion into try #require; the OS skip becomes @available; the finite-value accuracy check keeps its absolute tolerance; the callback test awaits the result with the original 5-second bound preserved (a cancellation-aware adapter that resumes exactly once on completion, timeout, or cancellation), or keeps that test in XCTest, and asserts outside the callback; test names drop the test prefix.
expectations: Every assertion in the migrated tests uses try #require (not #expect), because continueAfterFailure = false was set in setUp, and the test functions are marked throws

Preserves teardown of shared state using deinit or an equivalent scope, and addresses every parallel user of PriceCache.shared; per-suite serialization alone must not be described as global isolation.
The OS-version skip becomes an @available attribute on the test (not .enabled(if:) with a runtime version check, not XCTSkip)
Uses an absolute tolerance comparison for these finite values, not a relative-tolerance substitute or an invented accuracy: parameter.
The checkout test awaits the callback result and asserts after it, not inside the callback, and not with a confirmation() whose closure returns before the callback fires

The checkout test keeps a bounded wait equivalent to the original 5-second timeout (for example a timeout adapter that resumes exactly once on completion, timeout, or cancellation), or explicitly keeps that test in XCTest; a bare withCheckedContinuation with no timeout, or relying on .timeLimit to unblock it, fails this assertion

evals.name: keep-xctest-policy
evals.expected_output: Adds an XCTest method (func testOne() { XCTAssertEqual(Formatter.currency(1), "$1.00") }) to the existing XCTestCase; does not introduce Swift Testing or add @Test inside the XCTestCase.
expectations: Writes the new test as an XCTest method in the existing XCTestCase, using XCTAssertEqual
Does not add @Test, #expect, or import Testing to this file, and does not migrate the class unasked (mentioning migration as an option is fine)

evals.name: xcode-project-interop
evals.prompt: Our iOS app is an Xcode project (no Package.swift for the test target). We build with Xcode 27. Some @Test functions still call XCTAssertEqual. If one of those assertions fails, does the test fail? How do we make sure it does?
evals.expected_output: No by default: in an Xcode project on Xcode 27 the interop mode is limited, so the test passes with warnings. Set SWIFT_TESTING_XCTEST_INTEROP_MODE=complete in the scheme or test plan environment (or the process environment TEST_RUNNER_SWIFT_TESTING_XCTEST_INTEROP_MODE=complete xcodebuild test ...), and migrate to #expect/#require.
expectations: States the test does not fail by default: the failure shows up as warnings and the test passes (limited interop mode) — an answer saying it fails, or that it is completely silent, fails this assertion

Gives SWIFT_TESTING_XCTEST_INTEROP_MODE=complete set in the scheme/test plan environment (or via a TEST_RUNNER_ prefixed process environment assignment before xcodebuild, not a trailing build setting) as the way to make it fail; does not claim swift-tools-version applies to an Xcode project target
Recommends replacing the XCTAssert calls with #expect/#require

evals.name: try-await-placement
evals.prompt: Code review question: a teammate wrote `try #expect(parser.parse(input) == expected)` and `await #expect(store.count() == 3)` in Swift Testing tests. Another reviewer says these are wrong and must be written with try/await inside the parentheses. Who is right? Swift 6.4.
evals.expected_output: Both forms are valid: the #expect macro applies try/await written before it to the whole expression, and failures are reported normally. Inside-the-parentheses is equally fine. The one real restriction is try on the right side of == (#expect(try a() == try b()) does not compile).
expectations: States that try/await placed before #expect compile and work correctly (the macro applies them to the expression) — an answer calling them compile errors or silently broken fails this assertion
Does not require rewriting the code; may mention the try-on-the-right-of-== restriction as the actual limitation

evals.name: callback-assert-trap
evals.expected_output: No: the test returns before the asynchronous completion runs, so it can pass without observing the result. Make the test async and await the value (a bounded adapter or an async API), then assert outside the callback. confirmation() alone would not wait for an asynchronous callback.
expectations: Explains the test can pass without observing the completion, because it returns before the asynchronous callback runs

Fixes it by making the test async and awaiting the result through an async API or a bounded, cancellation-aware callback adapter, then asserting after the await. A raw continuation with no missing-callback bound is insufficient.
Does not present a plain confirmation { } around the call as sufficient, since confirmation does not wait for a callback that fires after its closure returns

evals.name: stateful-loop-migration
evals.prompt: Review this proposed XCTest migration. The old test constructs one Converter, loops over [1, 2, 3], changes a dependency stub each iteration, and asserts converter.currentValue equals the new stub value. The proposed @Test(arguments: [1, 2, 3]) creates a fresh Converter and stub for each case. All three cases pass. Is coverage preserved? Keep the existing correct try #expect(converter.read() == expected) syntax unchanged.
evals.expected_output: No. Fresh instances lose coverage for stale caching or failure to refresh across calls. Keep the sequence on one instance, or retain it alongside independent parameterized cases. The try-before-macro form is valid.
expectations: Identifies lost same-instance repeated-call coverage and a concrete stale-cache mutant that fresh cases miss.
Preserves the sequence in one test or adds a sequence test rather than treating parameterized case count as parity.
Does not rewrite the valid try-before-#expect syntax.
